method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Serotonin and noradrenaline re-uptake inhibitors SNRIs poisoning' (Last updated December 2020), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **SNRI self-poisoning is potentially life-threatening**: overdose frequently causes seizures, and large ingestions can cause cardiovascular toxicity.
claims.source_text: Deliberate or accidental self-poisoning with Serotonin and Noradrenaline Re-uptake Inhibitors [SNRIs] is potentially life-threatening … Overdoses frequently causes seizures and in large ingestions can cause cardiovascular toxicity
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Serotonin and noradrenaline re-uptake inhibitors SNRIs poisoning' (Last updated December 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Serotonin_and_noradrenaline_re-uptake_inhibitors_SNRIs_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **SNRIs:** atomoxetine, desvenlafaxine, duloxetine, reboxetine and venlafaxine. **Desvenlafaxine and venlafaxine come only as extended-release (ER) preparations.**
claims.source_text: Serotonin and Noradrenaline Re-uptake Inhibitors (SNRIs) include atomoxetine, desvenlafaxine, duloxetine, reboxetine and venlafaxine. Desvenlafaxine and venlafaxine are only available as extended-release (ER) preparations
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Serotonin and noradrenaline re-uptake inhibitors SNRIs poisoning' (Last updated December 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Serotonin_and_noradrenaline_re-uptake_inhibitors_SNRIs_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Venlafaxine carries the highest risk:** >2 g → seizures and serotonergic toxidrome · >5 g → 50% seizure risk · >8 g → cardiotoxicity. Under 800 mg is unlikely to cause significant toxicity.
claims.source_text: Venlafaxine having the highest risk of toxicity in overdose: ingestion of >2 g is associated with seizures and serotonergic toxidrome ingestion of >5 g is associated with a 50% risk of seizures ingestion of >8 g is associated with cardiotoxicity … ingestions of less than 800 mg of venlafaxine are unlikely to cause significant toxicity
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Serotonin and noradrenaline re-uptake inhibitors SNRIs poisoning' (Last updated December 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Serotonin_and_noradrenaline_re-uptake_inhibitors_SNRIs_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Symptoms usually start within 4 hours but may be delayed up to 16 hours with ER products**, usually resolving within 24 hours. ⚠️ **Seizures can be delayed up to 16 hours**, especially with ER preparations.
claims.source_text: Symptoms usually begin within 4 hours of consumption, but may be delayed up to 16 hours (with ER preparations) and usually resolve within 24 hours … Seizures may be delayed up to 16 hours following overdose, particularly following overdose with extended release preparations
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Serotonin and noradrenaline re-uptake inhibitors SNRIs poisoning' (Last updated December 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Serotonin_and_noradrenaline_re-uptake_inhibitors_SNRIs_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **High risk of serotonin syndrome with co-ingested serotonergic agents** — note tramadol and tapentadol have a weak SNRI effect.
claims.source_text: There is a high risk of serotonin syndrome if other serotonergic agents are co-ingested (NB Tramadol and tapentadol have weak SNRI effect)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Serotonin and noradrenaline re-uptake inhibitors SNRIs poisoning' (Last updated December 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Serotonin_and_noradrenaline_re-uptake_inhibitors_SNRIs_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess:** every deliberate self-poisoning · any symptomatic child · any ingestion of unknown quantity · any ingestion above the threshold below.
claims.source_text: All children with deliberate self-poisoning Any symptomatic child Acute ingestion of unknown quantity Children who have ingested doses greater than threshold for assessment
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Serotonin and noradrenaline re-uptake inhibitors SNRIs poisoning' (Last updated December 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Serotonin_and_noradrenaline_re-uptake_inhibitors_SNRIs_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Accidental-ingestion thresholds:** venlafaxine ≥12.5 mg/kg · desvenlafaxine ≥8.75 mg/kg · atomoxetine, duloxetine, reboxetine — toxic dose unknown, consult a toxicologist. **Not for adolescents or adults.**
claims.source_text: Venlafaxine ≥12.5 mg/kg Desvenlafaxine ≥8.75 mg/kg Atomoxetine, duloxetine, reboxetine Toxic dose is unknown – consult toxicologist … *Note these values do not apply to adolescents or adults (please discuss with toxicologist)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Serotonin and noradrenaline re-uptake inhibitors SNRIs poisoning' (Last updated December 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Serotonin_and_noradrenaline_re-uptake_inhibitors_SNRIs_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examination may show dysphoria, anxiety, mydriasis, tremor, tachycardia and hypertension.** ⚠️ **Coma or a significantly reduced conscious state is uncommon** — suspect a co-ingestant or another cause.
claims.source_text: May reveal dysphoria, anxiety, mydriasis, tremor, tachycardia and hypertension … Coma or significantly reduced conscious state is not common in SNRI overdose – this suggests co-ingestion or an alternative cause
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Serotonin and noradrenaline re-uptake inhibitors SNRIs poisoning' (Last updated December 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Serotonin_and_noradrenaline_re-uptake_inhibitors_SNRIs_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hypotension and dysrhythmias occur only after large venlafaxine ingestions; atomoxetine can prolong the QT.**
claims.source_text: Hypotension and cardiac dysrhythmias only occur following large ingestions of Venlafaxine. Atomoxetine can cause QT prolongation
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Serotonin and noradrenaline re-uptake inhibitors SNRIs poisoning' (Last updated December 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Serotonin_and_noradrenaline_re-uptake_inhibitors_SNRIs_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Hyperthermia signals severe serotonin syndrome** — it only occurs with co-ingested serotonergic drugs (e.g. SSRIs, MAOIs, some TCAs) — **and must be treated immediately.**
claims.source_text: Hyperthermia is a sign of severe serotonin syndrome which only occurs if there is co-ingestion of other serotonergically active drugs (eg SSRI, MAOIs some TCAs) … Hyperthermia is a sign of severe serotonin syndrome and should be immediately treated.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Serotonin and noradrenaline re-uptake inhibitors SNRIs poisoning' (Last updated December 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Serotonin_and_noradrenaline_re-uptake_inhibitors_SNRIs_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **ECG on presentation, then 6-hourly until discharge.** Large ingestion or prolonged QRS/QTc: continuous cardiac monitoring and 2-hourly ECGs. Deliberate self-poisoning: blood glucose and paracetamol level.
claims.source_text: ECG on presentation and ECG 6 hourly until discharge … If large ingestion or prolonged QRS or QTc ongoing cardiac monitoring and 2 hourly ECG is recommended … blood glucose and paracetamol level in deliberate self-poisoning
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Serotonin and noradrenaline re-uptake inhibitors SNRIs poisoning' (Last updated December 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Serotonin_and_noradrenaline_re-uptake_inhibitors_SNRIs_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Large ingestion: early intubation and ventilation** (discuss with a toxicologist).
claims.source_text: Early intubation and ventilation is indicated if large ingestion (Discuss with toxicologist)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Serotonin and noradrenaline re-uptake inhibitors SNRIs poisoning' (Last updated December 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Serotonin_and_noradrenaline_re-uptake_inhibitors_SNRIs_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Activated charcoal only after toxicologist discussion**, but consider it for alert, co-operative patients with large ingestions. **Whole bowel irrigation may be considered for venlafaxine >5 g within 4 hours.**
claims.source_text: Activated charcoal should only be administered following discussion with toxicologist but should be considered in alert, co-operative patients who have large ingestions … Whole bowel irrigation may be considered for venlafaxine ingestions >5 g within 4 hours of the estimated ingestion time.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Serotonin and noradrenaline re-uptake inhibitors SNRIs poisoning' (Last updated December 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Serotonin_and_noradrenaline_re-uptake_inhibitors_SNRIs_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Seizures: benzodiazepines. Avoid phenytoin and fentanyl.**
claims.source_text: Treat seizures with benzodiazepines Avoid phenytoin and fentanyl
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Serotonin and noradrenaline re-uptake inhibitors SNRIs poisoning' (Last updated December 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Serotonin_and_noradrenaline_re-uptake_inhibitors_SNRIs_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Serotonin syndrome can also be treated with titrated IV benzodiazepines** (discuss with a toxicologist).
claims.source_text: Serotonin syndrome can also be treated with titrated intravenous benzodiazepines (Discuss with toxicologist)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Serotonin and noradrenaline re-uptake inhibitors SNRIs poisoning' (Last updated December 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Serotonin_and_noradrenaline_re-uptake_inhibitors_SNRIs_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Observe every deliberate self-poisoning, and any accidental ingestion needing assessment, for at least 16 hours and/or until symptom-free.** After >5 g of venlafaxine, observe **at least 24 hours**.
claims.source_text: all children with deliberate self-poisoning or accidental ingestion requiring assessment should be observed for a minimum of 16 hours and/or until symptom free … Children who ingest >5 g of venlafaxine are at increased risk of delayed seizures. Observe them for at least 24 hours after ingestion
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Serotonin and noradrenaline re-uptake inhibitors SNRIs poisoning' (Last updated December 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Serotonin_and_noradrenaline_re-uptake_inhibitors_SNRIs_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Large ingestion, cardiotoxicity or QT prolongation: continuous ECG monitoring and serial 12-lead ECGs** for at least 6 hours (immediate release), 16 hours (extended release) or 24 hours (venlafaxine >5 g).
claims.source_text: Children with large ingestions, cardiotoxicity or QT-interval prolongation following SNRI poisoning require continuous ECG monitoring and serial 12-lead ECGs for: at least 6 hours after ingestion of an immediate-release preparation at least 16 hours after ingestion of extended-release preparation at least 24 hours after ingestion of >5 g of venlafaxine
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Serotonin and noradrenaline re-uptake inhibitors SNRIs poisoning' (Last updated December 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Serotonin_and_noradrenaline_re-uptake_inhibitors_SNRIs_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Asymptomatic accidental ingestion below the assessment threshold can be observed at home.** Consider admission for every intentional overdose.
claims.source_text: Children with accidental ingestion can be observed at home if asymptomatic and dose is below that requiring medical assessment … Admission should be considered for all children and young people with an intentional overdose.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Serotonin and noradrenaline re-uptake inhibitors SNRIs poisoning' (Last updated December 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Serotonin_and_noradrenaline_re-uptake_inhibitors_SNRIs_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Large ingestions and severe serotonin syndrome are managed in a paediatric ICU.**
claims.source_text: Children who have large ingestions or develop severe serotonin syndrome should be managed in a paediatric ICU.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Serotonin and noradrenaline re-uptake inhibitors SNRIs poisoning' (Last updated December 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Serotonin_and_noradrenaline_re-uptake_inhibitors_SNRIs_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when GCS and ECG are normal** and the child has stayed asymptomatic for at least 6 hours (immediate release), 16 hours (extended release) or 24 hours (venlafaxine >5 g).
claims.source_text: GCS is normal ECG is normal … For most SNRI poisonings, children can be discharged if they remain asymptomatic for: at least 6 hours after ingestion of an immediate-release SNRI preparation at least 16 hours after ingestion of an extended-release SNRI preparation at least 24 hours after ingestion of >5 g of venlafaxine
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Serotonin and noradrenaline re-uptake inhibitors SNRIs poisoning' (Last updated December 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Serotonin_and_noradrenaline_re-uptake_inhibitors_SNRIs_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23
